summary:
Summary:
TASK-003 (view individual peak information) meets all nine acceptance criteria. Each peak card now has a "View details" button, labelled "View details for <name>", that opens a modal `<dialog>`. The dialog content comes from a pure function, `createPeakDetails`, in `src/peak-utils.js`. A separate controller, `src/peak-details-controller.js`, handles opening, closing, Escape, focus return and toggling. Toggling from the dialog uses the same `setPeakToggled` path as the cards, so the card, overall progress and region progress all update. `npm test` ran 93 tests: 93 passed, 0 failed, exit code 0. That count includes 10 headless-browser tests, which really ran rather than being skipped. They check keyboard focus, the inert page behind the dialog, live progress updates, and layout at 360px and on desktop.

Issues:
- No acceptance criterion failed. One non-blocking cleanup item: three untracked stray files are in the working tree and should be removed before commit. They are a file named `` {`n `` at the project root (probably a leftover from a broken PowerShell command), `.ai/debug.tmp.mjs` and `.ai/test-out.tmp`.
- No peak in `data/peaks.json` has a grid reference, so the "with grid reference" case is only tested with made-up data (`{ ...peak, gridRef: 'NH 019 718' }`). This meets the criterion and does not add anything to the dataset.

Tests:
- `npm test`: Total 93, Passed 93, Failed 0, exit code 0. The only warnings were npm complaining about the Node v24 version.
- AC1 (accessible details control): every card has a real `<button>` with `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-label="View details for <name>"`. A unit test checks all 100 cards, and a browser test opens the dialog with the keyboard.
- AC2 (number, name, region, height, status): unit tests check `createPeakDetails` against every dataset peak, and a browser test checks the text actually shown in the dialog.
- AC3 (grid reference only when present): the row appears when a grid reference exists. With an undefined, empty, whitespace-only or null value there is no row and no placeholder text such as "undefined", "null", "N/A" or "Unknown". A browser test confirms no grid reference text appears for a real peak.
- AC4 (toggle from the dialog updates everything): a browser test marks a peak complete and then unmarks it from the dialog. It checks the card's completed class, the overall text changing from "1% complete (1/100…)" back to "0%", the region count going 1/N and back to 0/N, and the localStorage save.
- AC5 (closing and focus return): browser tests close the dialog with Escape and with the visible Close button. In both cases focus returns to the same peak's "View details" button. This also works after the peak is unmarked while the list is filtered to "Completed", because that peak's card stays pinned in the list.
- AC6 (focus moves in and stays in): when the dialog opens, focus goes to the Close button. Eight Tab presses and eight Shift+Tab presses never reach page content. A mouse click on a card behind the dialog does not toggle it.
- AC7 (mobile and desktop): at 360×740 there is no horizontal overflow, the dialog fits the screen, both buttons are at least 44px tall, and the longest peak name wraps. On desktop the dialog is centred, between 300 and 520px wide, and fits vertically. CSS rule tests also pass.
- AC8 (pure function with tests): `createPeakDetails` is in `src/peak-utils.js` and does not touch the DOM. Tests cover purity, HTML escaping, and peaks with and without a grid reference.
- AC9 (nothing broken): all earlier suites still pass (dataset, progress, completion, filtering, cards, region progress, server, responsive), and `npm test` exits with code 0.

QA OUTCOME: PASSED
